defs.def: a story long enough to fill a complete book, in which the characters and events are usually imaginary （长篇）小说adjective

ex.s: Not long ago, my fifth-grade son Kevin asked me about the meaning of a word in a novel.
ex.t: 不久前，我上五年级的儿子凯文问我一本小说里一个词的意思。

ex.s: A novel design approach to gardening has been gaining in popularity worldwide.
ex.t: 一种新颖的园艺设计方法正在全球范围内越来越受欢迎。

ex.s: Elizabeth Sims analyzes the final chapters of five great novels to see what key points they include and how you can adapt them for your work.
ex.t: 伊丽莎白·西姆斯分析了五部伟大小说的最后章节，看看它们包含哪些要点，以及你如何将其改编运用到自己的作品中。

ex.s: To discuss a novel.
ex.t: 讨论一部小说。

ex.s: Renewed contact with a novel or a poem can activate the search for a better knowledge of the self.
ex.t: 意义是通过社会互动的过程产生的，而非计算过程，这种互动塑造了我们头脑中符号的内容。

ex.s: To collect details for writing novels.
ex.t: 为写小说收集细节。

ex.s: When I decided to pursue a postgraduate degree, I wanted to develop a novel research programme and quickly establish myself as an independent scientist.
ex.t: 当我决定攻读研究生学位时，我想开发一个新颖的研究项目，并迅速确立自己作为独立科学家的地位。

ex.s: Klein, a noted historian of technology, spins a narrative so lively that at times it reads like a novel.
ex.t: Klein是一位著名的技术史学家，他讲述的叙事如此生动，有时读起来像小说。

ex.s: If the only reading you ever do is the novel or magazine, the speed at which you read -probably does not matter very much.
ex.t: 如果你唯一的阅读就是小说或杂志，那么你阅读的速度可能并不太重要。

ex.s: In a novel.
ex.t: 在一本小说中。

ex.s: Even if this method of timekeeping is novel in its particulars，early agricultural societies also connected time to natural phenomena．In pre-Classical Greece，for instance，people“corrected”official calendars by shifting dates forward or backward to reflect the change of season．Temporal connection to the environment was vital to their survival．Likewise，river time and other timekeeping systems we're developing may encourage environmental awareness．
ex.t: 即便这种计时方式在细节上很新颖，早期的农业社会也将时间与自然现象联系起来。例如在前古典时期的希腊，人们会通过把日期向前或向后调整来“修正”官方历法，以反映季节的变化。与环境的时间联系对他们的生存至关重要。同样，我们正在开发的河流时间和其他计时系统或许也能唤起人们的环保意识。

ex.s: Purchase her novels.
ex.t: 购买她的小说。

ex.s: Or maybe you end up switching your attention away from novels, and discover the history of romantic poets in England.
ex.t: 或者你可能最终把注意力从小说上转移开，发现了英国浪漫派诗人的历史。

ex.s: reading novels is a way to learn about a historical period
ex.t: 读小说是了解某个历史时期的一种方式

ex.s: Remember that Thomas Costain was 57 when he published his first novel, and that Grandma Moses showed her first pictures when she was 78.
ex.t: 记住，托马斯·科斯坦57岁时才出版了他的第一部小说，而摩西奶奶78岁时才展出了她的第一批画作。

ex.s: This is an excellent fantasy novel from one of the best storytellers around.
ex.t: 这是当代最出色讲故事人之一创作的优秀奇幻小说。

ex.s: Most of my reading through primary， middle and high school was factual reading． I read for knowledge， and to make A's on my tests． Occasionally， I would read a novel that was assigned， but I didn't enjoy this type of reading． I liked facts， things that are concrete． I thought anything abstract left too much room for argument．
ex.t: 在小学、初中和高中阶段，我的大部分阅读都是事实性阅读。我为获取知识而读，为了在考试中拿A。偶尔，我也会读老师指定的小说，但我并不喜欢这种阅读。我喜欢事实，喜欢具体的东西。我认为任何抽象的事物都留下了太多争论的空间。

ex.s: Yet， now that I'm growing and the world I once knew as being so simple is becoming more complex， I find myself needing a way to escape． By opening a novel， I can leave behind my burdens and enter into a wonderful and mysterious world where I am now a new character． In these worlds I can become anyone． I don't have to write down what happened or what technique the author was using when he or she wrote this． I just read to relax．
ex.t: 然而，随着我渐渐长大，曾经以为如此简单的世界变得越来越复杂，我发现自己需要一种逃避的方式。打开一本小说，我就能抛开烦恼，进入一个奇妙而神秘的世界，在那里我成为一个新的角色。在这些世界里我可以成为任何人。我不必记下发生了什么，也不必分析作者写作时运用了什么技巧。我阅读只是为了放松。

ex.s: （4）The author takes novel reading as a way to     ．
ex.t: （4）作者把读小说当作一种___的方式。

ex.s: In 1812, the year Charles Dickens was born, there were 66 novels published in Britain.
ex.t: 1812年，查尔斯·狄更斯出生的那一年，英国出版了66部小说。

ex.s: People had been writing novels for a century—most experts date the first novel to Robinson Crusoe in 1719—
ex.t: 人们写小说已有一个世纪——大多数学者把第一部小说定为1719年的《鲁滨逊漂流记》——

ex.s: Many works of fiction appeared without the names of the authors, often with something like “By a lady.”Novels, for the most part, were looked upon as silly, immoral, or just plain bad.
ex.t: 许多小说作品出版时没有作者名字，往往只署类似“一位女士著”。小说在很大程度上被看作愚蠢、不道德，或者干脆就是烂。

ex.s: In 1870, when Dickens died, the world mourned him as its first professional writer and publisher, famous and beloved, who had led an explosion in both the publication of novels and their readership and whose characters — from Oliver Twist to Tiny Tim— were held up as moral touchstones.
ex.t: 1870年狄更斯去世时，世界哀悼这位首位职业作家和出版人，他声名显赫、深受爱戴，引领了小说出版与读者群的爆发式增长，其笔下人物——从奥利弗·崔斯特到小蒂姆——被视为道德试金石。

ex.s: Some 60,000 novels were published during the Victorian age, from 1837 to1901; today a casual reader might be able to name a half-dozen of them.
ex.t: 在维多利亚时代，从1837年到1901年，出版了约6万本小说；今天，一个随便的读者也许可以将其中的六分之一命名。

ex.s: Which of the following best describes British novels in the 18th century?
ex.t: 以下哪项最能描述18世纪英国小说？

ex.s: To introduce an English novel.
ex.t: 为了介绍一部英国小说。

ex.s: The road novel, the road movie, these are the most typical American ideas, born of abundant petrol, cheap cars and a never-ending interstate highway system, the largest public works project in history.
ex.t: 公路小说、公路电影，这些是最典型的美国观念，诞生于充足的汽油、便宜的汽车和永无止境的洲际高速公路系统——史上最大的公共工程。

ex.s: To understand this, think of a graph where the vertical lines quantify how many movie tickets. you can buy and where the horizontal lines do the same for crime novels.
ex.t: 要理解这点，想象一张图，竖线量化你能买多少电影票，横线对犯罪小说做同样的事。

ex.s: You like going to the movies and reading crime novels and you have $ 150 to spend, In the example below, assume that each movie costs $10 and each crime novel costs $15.
ex.t: 你喜欢看电影和读犯罪小说，有150美元可花。在下面的例子中，假设每部电影10美元，每本犯罪小说15美元。

ex.s: You can also graph the other extreme — all crime novels and no movies.
ex.t: 所以你在水平轴数字10处做一个标记。

ex.s: Since crime novels in the example cost $15 and you have $150 available, if you spend all the available money crime novels, you can buy 10.
ex.t: 由于示例中的犯罪小说售价为$ 15 ，而您可以使用$ 150 ，因此如果您花费所有可用的货币犯罪小说，则可以购买10本。

ex.s: Any combination of movies and crime novels that falls below the budget line is affordable.
ex.t: 任何电影和犯罪小说的组合，只要落在预算线以下就是负担得起的。

ex.s: Assume that each movie costs 10 and each crime novel costs, $15, you have $150.Which is RIGHT according to this passage?
ex.t: 假设每部电影10元，每本犯罪小说15元，你有150元。根据这篇文章哪项是对的？

ex.s: The maximum number of crime novels you can buy is 15.
ex.t: 你最多可以买15本犯罪小说。

ex.s: You can buy 7 crime novels and, see 5 movies.
ex.t: 你可以买7部犯罪小说 看5部电影

ex.s: You can buy 7 crime novels and see 4 movies.
ex.t: 你可以买下7部犯罪小说，看4部电影。

ex.s: When he was writing his novels, Charles Dickens would act out the parts of the characters, He’d make faces in the mirror, and change his voice for each character.
ex.t: 查尔斯·狄更斯写小说时，会表演角色的部分，对着镜子做鬼脸，并为每个角色变换声音。

ex.s: Background information The Secret Garden is a children's novel by British-American novelist Frances Hodgson Burnett.
ex.t: 背景信息 《秘密花园》是英美小说家弗朗西斯\u00b7霍奇森\u00b7伯内特写的一本儿童小说。

ex.s: Tolkien (1892-1973) was an English writer, poet and university professor, best known as the author of some of the world’s most popular high-fantasy novels.
ex.t: 托尔金（1892-1973）是一位英国作家、诗人和大学教授，最以创作了全球最受欢迎的一些高阶奇幻小说而闻名。

ex.s: His novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings have been made into films.
ex.t: 他的小说《霍比特人》和《指环王》已被改编成电影。

ex.s: Background information The Lord of the Rings is an epic high-fantasy novel written by J.
ex.t: 背景信息 《指环王》是 J. 托尔金创作的一部史诗级高阶奇幻小说。

ex.s: The Lord of the Rings was published in three volumes in 1954 and 1955, and has become one of the world's best-selling novel 2 Every Christmas, an envelope with a North Pole stamp arrived.
ex.t: 《指环王》于 1954 年和 1955 年分三卷出版，已成为世界上最畅销的小说之一 2 每年圣诞节，一封带着北极邮戳的信封都会如期而至。
